Do not add Redis. This system has one writer, restores state from SQLite, and has no cross-host coordination requirement. Redis adds a failure domain and an operational dependency without solving a constraint you actually have.

Where Redis would be the answer: multiple writer processes, a shared cache or queue across hosts, or persistence guarantees beyond what SQLite gives you. None of those apply here.

If the motivation is performance, measure first. A single Elixir process can hold hot state in ETS or GenServer memory with no new infrastructure at all.
